summary.text: Cleavage is the tendency of a crystal to split along definite flat planes set by its structure.
These planes exist because atoms sit in a regular pattern, and where bonds in some directions are weaker, the crystal breaks along them.
Cleavage is a traditional clue for identifying minerals, and the angles between cleavage planes can be diagnostic.

facts.label: Classic example
facts.value: Mica, which peels into thin sheets

facts.label: Salt's cleavage
facts.value: Cubic: broken halite forms more cubes

items.prompt: You smash a large crystal of table salt with a hammer. What shapes do the pieces tend to take?

options.label: Thin flat sheets
Smaller cubes
Rounded grains
Long needles

items.explain: Halite has three cleavage planes meeting at right angles, so broken crystals form more cubes.

items.prompt: Graphite's bonds within each layer are stronger than diamond's bonds. Why, then, does graphite feel slippery?

options.label: It contains trapped oil
Its atoms are much lighter than diamond's
Its surface is coated in water
Its layers are held together by weak bonds

items.explain: Each layer is joined to the next by a weak van der Waals bond, so layers shear apart with little force.

items.prompt: A mineralogist finds that every sample of one mineral splits along the same planes, while another mineral breaks that way only in some samples. Which describes the second mineral?

options.label: Parting caused by defects in those samples
Perfect cleavage
Basal cleavage
A mineral that is too hard to break

items.explain: Cleavage appears in all samples of a mineral, while parting comes from growth defects and is found only in samples that have them.

items.prompt: Every crystal has some tendency to split along atomic planes. Why do some minerals, like corundum, show no cleavage?

options.label: They are not truly crystals at all
They are too soft to split cleanly
Their bonds differ too little by direction
They only split apart under great heat

items.explain: If the differences between directions are not large enough, the mineral will not display cleavage.

items.prompt: A crystal splits cleanly along three planes that do not meet at right angles. Which type of cleavage is this?

options.label: Cubic
Octahedral
Prismatic
Rhombohedral

items.explain: Three planes not at 90 degrees is rhombohedral cleavage, as in calcite; three at 90 degrees would be cubic.

items.prompt: A geologist has two minerals that each split along two planes. How could the cleavage help tell a pyroxene from an amphibole?

options.label: Count how many planes each has
Measure the angle between the planes
Check whether the planes feel slippery
See which one peels into sheets

items.explain: Pyroxene cleavage planes meet near 90°, amphibole planes at about 56° and 124°, so the angle is diagnostic.
